title: Letting My Viewers Fix My Stock Prediction Program | Python LSTM Stock Predictor

owner_label.reasoning: Deliberately chosen as the adversarial/bad-bucket example. The approach (LSTM/tree ML on price history, sentiment, technical features to predict next-day returns) is undermined by market efficiency: any exploitable pattern in public price/sentiment data is already priced in by faster, better-capitalized institutional actors. The incremental fixes (early stopping, log-return targets, permutation importance, time-decayed features) are legitimate ML engineering but do not address why the strategy can't work -- the model backtests against random-portfolio noise bands and reportedly still can't clear them.

claims.claim_text: builds an LSTM trained on price history, sentiment, and technical features to predict next-day stock direction/return
acknowledges any exploitable pattern in public price/sentiment data is likely already priced in by faster, better-capitalized institutional actors (market efficiency)
compares the ML model against both a buy-and-hold S&P benchmark and a band of random buy/sell portfolios; the model must beat the random noise band to be considered working
reports the model still cannot clearly beat the random-portfolio noise band
adds early stopping (halt after 10-15 epochs without validation improvement) to reduce overfitting/training time
switches the target from binary up/down to next-day log return, to rank opportunities by expected magnitude
adds permutation importance for feature importance and time-decayed features
